validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, well-documented intrastate NC gas transmission project, confirmed by FIVE independent sources spanning 2014-2020: (1) Franklin County Economic Development Commission meeting minutes, 2014-07-10 (franklincountync.gov), quoting PSNC's Jerry O'Keeffe directly: 'PSNC is proposing a new transmission line (known as T-030) through Franklin County'; (2) landownerattorneys.com law-firm blog, dated 2014-07-16 (confirmed via schema.org datePublished), describing the same PSNC Franklin/Wake pipeline (20-29 mi, $35-45M preliminary estimate); (3) TRC Companies press release, 2017-05-12, announcing a $2.5M engineering/construction-support contract for 'PSNC Energy...40-mile Franklin and Wake County Extension Project,' a 20-inch transmission line, construction expected fall 2017, completion summer 2019; (4) Pipeline & Gas Journal 'Planned Projects' PDF (PN1018, Oct 2018 rev, pgj-wp-media/S3): 'PSNC ENERGY CO. - Project: T-030 Gas Pipeline Extension, Length: 37 miles, Diameter: 20 inches, Location: Franklinton, NC - Clayton, NC, Completion: 2Q 2019...System will terminate at the Clayton supply interchange facility which will also serve as a future supply interchange with the planned Atlantic Coast Pipeline' -- this literally names 'T-030' and matches the GEM-recorded 37 mi value exactly; (5) Wayback-archived gcpa.net (Gulf Coast LLC, a right-of-way acquisition contractor), captured 2018-02-06 and again through 2020: 'PSNC Energy T-030 pipeline Franklin and Wake County, North Carolina...purchase of a fifty foot right of way for a 23 mile natural gas pipeline' -- also literally names T-030. Sources 3 and 2 do not use the literal string 'T-030' but are identified as the same physical project beyond reasonable doubt by the unique combination of owner (PSNC Energy/SCANA), the two counties (Franklin and Wake, NC), and the 20-inch diameter, which sources 4 and 5 (which DO say 'T-030') independently corroborate. CLASSIFICATION: correctly classified as a gas transmission pipeline (not gathering/gas processing) -- source 4 explicitly: 'Type: Project includes pipeline construction,' a extension terminating at a supply interchange facility that was also to interconnect with the (since-cancelled) Atlantic Coast Pipeline. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 41-row roster -- no other row describes this project; P0311 Buncombe County Pipeline is a different, unrelated western-NC project (Arden, near Asheville) with no overlap in counties or owner. SPEC CAVEAT (not a material concern): the pipeline's length estimate evolved visibly across its multi-year planning history -- 20-29 mi (2014, pre-route-selection), 40 mi (May 2017, TRC contract announcement), 23 mi (2018-2020 static ROW-acquisition-firm listing, likely describing only the acquired ROW segment or an interim scope), and finally 37 mi (Oct 2018 PGJ trade press, matching the value currently recorded in GEM). This reflects normal project-scope refinement as the route was finalized (per source 1, route selection was not expected until 2016), not a data-quality problem with the recorded 37 mi figure, which is the latest and most detailed (paired with exact diameter and termini) of the five. STATUS: the project's cancellation is not independently, directly sourced anywhere found (no article states 'T-030 cancelled') -- see the status_reviews object below, which formalizes this as an inferred dormancy conclusion rather than a directly-evidenced one. ROUTE CHECK: ../GOIT-GGIT-pipeline-routes/data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P0355.geojson is a single LineString, 107 points, first point [-78.476097, 36.079598] (~2.5 mi from Franklinton, NC town center, consistent with a route beginning near Franklinton), last point [-78.517825, 35.672527] (~3-4 mi northwest of Clayton, NC town center -- consistent with terminating at a specific facility near but not in downtown Clayton, matching source 4's description of the line ending at 'the Clayton supply interchange facility' rather than the town itself). The route is plausible and consistent with the sourced termini; not flagged as a mismatch.

The last dated evidence of active development is the Oct 2018 PGJ trade-press entry targeting 2Q 2019 completion; no source after that date mentions the project at all, including the 2019-10-20 Wayback capture of the ROW-acquisition contractor's page (gcpa.net), which is textually identical to the 2018-02-06 capture and shows no progress update. The project's planned interconnect, the Atlantic Coast Pipeline, was itself cancelled in July 2020, removing one of T-030's stated purposes. This silence is the basis for a dormancy-rule INFERENCE of cancellation (formalized in the status_reviews object below, verdict='stale', ShelvedCancelledType='inferred'), not a directly-sourced fact -- per standing rule 2, no fabricated ref is attached to an inference. Leaving this unit UNRESOLVED rather than citing a source that does not actually say 'cancelled.'
